chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I doubt while I am prostrating, so I do not know if I have bowed or not. He said: 'You have bowed, proceed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when one doubts if they bowed during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi establishes the principle of 'istishab al-bara'ah' (presumption of innocence) in ritual purity, where doubt during prostration is resolved by assuming the preceding ruku' was completed. It highlights the Shia juristic preference for ease and continuity in prayer, contrasting with stricter views that might require re-prostration or restarting the prayer. The ruling underscores the reliability of the worshipper's initial state unless proven otherwise, reflecting the practical application of doubt in daily worship.
